title: Culture, with a point of view.
name: District Culture
intro: An editorial voice for a brand that lives where people go out, discover things, and talk about them afterwards.
paragraphs: We help run District Culture end to end, shaping how District joins conversations about culture, trends, and the internet. The work moves between pop culture, social commentary, intergenerational stories, and cultural movements in India and beyond.

Fiction, non-fiction, opinion, and entertainment share the same space. From working with Kevin Hart to revisiting Zayed Khan’s Lakshman, the task is to keep the voice playful, sharp, and recognisably District.
insight: A useful editorial voice gives a brand something to say beyond its next announcement.

title: An announcement worth watching.
name: District launch films
intro: New launches, told through familiar stories instead of feature lists.
paragraphs: A nostalgic salon campaign with Zayed Khan. A sport-inspired food film with Tilak Varma. The launch of District Play for booking sports venues. The District Dining Carnival. Each brief called for its own world and its own reason to watch.
We built story-led films that let the announcement sit naturally inside the idea. The aim: make the launch understandable without letting the message overwhelm the entertainment.
insight: When the story does the work, the announcement has room to land.

title: A city, through its kitchens.
name: In Your District
intro: Stories about the chefs, cuisines, restaurants, and people that give a city its flavour.
paragraphs: Across Delhi, Mumbai, and Bangalore, we create regular content around restaurants, events, and the people behind the food. The series moves from celebrated chefs such as Gaggan Anand and Prateek Sadhu to local kitchens with stories of their own.
The approach stays curious and community-led. A restaurant is a way into a place: the people who run it, the food they care about, and the city around them.
insight: The most interesting food story often begins with a person.

title: The festival beyond the stage.
name: Rolling Loud India
services: Content strategy · On-ground production · Live edits
intro: Artist encounters, audience energy, and festival stories built for the moment and the days after.
paragraphs: We handled end-to-end on-ground production: vox pops, artist interactions, and event coverage. Selected assets were delivered live, bringing moments from the festival into the feed while they were happening.
The rest of the work followed a structured content calendar. Explainers and atmosphere-led edits extended the story after the event, giving the coverage a life beyond a single weekend.
insight: Live coverage has two rhythms: the moment itself, and the memory that follows.

title: Something to look forward to.
name: Only Fridays
intro: A rewards IP built around experiences people would want to tell a story about.
paragraphs: Only Fridays replaces the familiar cashback proposition with unexpected, culturally relevant rewards. We worked on an IP where the anticipation is part of the experience.

The possibilities ranged from a gameshow with Karan Johar to a house stocked with Dyson products and a Bangalore chef’s crawl with chefs from places such as Naru. Each reward became a premise, giving members a new reason to pay attention on Friday.
insight: A reward can be more than a transaction. It can be the start of a story.

title: First times. Full commitment.
name: First Time with Simba
intro: Joel D’Souza tries something completely new, with all the uncertainty that comes with it.
paragraphs: This multi-episode YouTube series follows first-time experiences: an overnight stay at a haunted fort, sailing, extreme food challenges, and entering a bodybuilding competition.
We built an entertainment format around humour, chaos, and genuine surprise. The show’s visual identity and distribution carried the premise across YouTube and Instagram.
insight: An unfamiliar situation gives a familiar personality somewhere new to go.

title: NRI life. No instruction manual.
name: Plus91
intro: A playful studio format that makes an unfamiliar brand feel easy to step into.
paragraphs: Plus91 invites people to guess different parts of NRI life: where someone lives, how long they have been abroad, and the experiences that connect them.
The long-form series is fast, studio-shot, and led by culture. It gives finance-adjacent content a friendly entry point through people, participation, and shared experiences.
insight: For a finance brand, the conversation can begin with the life around the money.

title: What it takes to make a home.
name: Journeys of Aspiration
services: Visual identity · Content strategy · International production
intro: Personal stories of building a life abroad, filmed across the UK and UAE.
paragraphs: Families, couples, founders, a Michelin-star chef, and a Formula 2 driver share how they built new homes, careers, and identities.
The series looks beyond nostalgia to the choices and work behind those lives. Mid-form stories and short-form extensions bring the same human perspective to different viewing habits.
insight: The story of moving away is also the story of building something new.

title: Make the unfamiliar feel familiar.
name: SuperYou Pro launch
intro: A cinematic introduction to a new performance-product category, starting with creatine.
paragraphs: We partnered on the launch of SuperYou Pro, creating a film that blended micro-fiction, vox pops, and product explanation.

The creative challenge was to introduce a complex supplement category in a way that felt entertaining, relatable, and easy to follow. The film brought explanation into the story instead of separating the two.
insight: Understanding comes more easily when the explanation earns your attention.

title: More room for women in sport.
name: The Sports Women
intro: An ongoing editorial platform spotlighting women athletes and sporting moments across India.
paragraphs: For Capri, we run The Sports Women across Instagram and YouTube. The coverage spans Olympic journeys, women’s cricket, and major tournaments.

Fast edits, opinion documentaries, vox pops, and social-first stories make space for both the headline and the person behind it. The work is built around a consistent, accessible place for women’s sport.
insight: Sport deserves a story between the highlights, too.

title: The business behind the bottle.
name: In d’you time
intro: A skincare brand lets the audience into the everyday work of building a company.
paragraphs: We created a YouTube series following d’you in real time: quick commerce, operations, packaging, demand, and growth. The material comes from the day-to-day decisions of the business.
The format moves away from conventional skincare content towards observational storytelling. Long-form episodes and short-form extensions share the same unvarnished view of work as it happens.
insight: The process can be the story, if you let people close enough to see it.

title: A launch with a little play.
name: COSMIX launch content
intro: Product-launch content in the brand’s own playful, transparent voice.
paragraphs: We developed launch assets for COSMIX’s multivitamin, pairing the core announcement with gamified formats that invited people into the conversation.
In one format, the team taste-tests protein flavours they would never make. Reactions to intentionally absurd combinations create an entertainment-first entry point into the brand’s world.
insight: A product conversation can make room for a sense of humour.

title: A show with a mind of its own.
name: Dumb Biryani
services: Original concept · Visual identity · Production · Experiential launch
intro: Arhaan Khan, Dev Raiyani, and Arush Verma turn the podcast format into an internet-first reality show.
paragraphs: We built Dumb Biryani end to end, giving it an intentionally lo-fi, anti-art visual language and a format that leaves space for the unexpected. Guests range from Neeraj Goyat to Bollywood paparazzi and the Fabulous Wives.
The launch took the show beyond the screen and into Mumbai, with a themed food truck and flyers. It is a Revolio original: a world we built, rather than a brief we were handed.
insight: An original format needs a personality that holds together on screen, in the feed, and out in the world.

title: One dialogue. One bucket. One mind reader.
name: Hold My Popcorn
intro: Suhani Shah takes film knowledge and a little mind-reading to the street.
paragraphs: We conceptualised a gamified vox-pop series in which a participant thinks of a famous dialogue from a film or show while trying to finish a bucket of popcorn.
Before the popcorn runs out, Suhani reads their cues and tries to guess the dialogue. A simple rule gives the street interaction a clock, a challenge, and a reveal.
insight: A clear game makes room for spontaneous entertainment.

title: Building a podcast from day one.
name: Sparx by Mukesh Bansal
intro: An ongoing creative partnership for Mukesh Bansal’s productivity and motivation podcast.
paragraphs: Revolio has been Sparx’s creative partner since day one, working across the brand, content, and growth of the show.
The partnership brings the different parts of a podcast’s presence together, from what an episode looks like to how its ideas travel beyond the full conversation.
insight: A show becomes recognisable when its content and identity move together.

title: Business school, beyond the brochure.
name: Mesa content IPs
intro: An inside view of campus life, pedagogy, and real-world startup experiences.
paragraphs: For Mesa School of Business, we built content IPs around the experiences of an institution focused on the next generation of startup founders.
The work connected the school’s digital presence to what actually happens there: how people learn, the ideas they test, and the startup experiences they encounter.
insight: Show what an education feels like, as well as what it offers.

title: Entrepreneurship, in conversation.
name: The Barbershop with Shantanu
intro: Revolio’s first entrepreneurial podcast, built from the beginning.
paragraphs: The Barbershop with Shantanu brought entrepreneurship into a conversational format. Revolio helped build the show from its earliest stage.
The wider work included Razorpreneur, a pan-India campus challenge that took entrepreneurial participation beyond the podcast.
insight: A conversation can become the starting point for a wider community.

title: A film’s story, beyond the screen.
name: 12th Fail release campaign
services: Creative strategy · Social media · Telegram marketing
intro: Social and Telegram marketing across the release cycle of Vidhu Vinod Chopra’s film.
paragraphs: Revolio led social media and Telegram marketing for 12th Fail, supporting the release through creative strategy and audience engagement.
The work followed the film’s release cycle and key milestones, giving its story of grit and perseverance a presence beyond the cinema.
insight: Release marketing is an ongoing conversation with an audience.

title: A digital presence that listens to the film.
name: All We Imagine As Light
intro: A platform-first marketing approach for a film with a quiet, evocative voice.
paragraphs: Revolio led the film’s platform-first marketing, working on digital visibility and sustained audience engagement.
The work centred the film’s distinct voice, shaping a digital presence around its character rather than imposing a generic release template.
insight: The campaign should make you want to enter the film’s world.

title: From set to screen to feed.
name: TEST
intro: Marketing material and on-set video assets for Netflix’s film TEST.
paragraphs: Revolio worked on marketing materials and video assets from the set of TEST.
The work extended the film’s world into material for its audience-facing campaign.
insight: What happens around the film can give audiences another way into it.
